Key.Original: Vehicle construction is enabled at FOBs as well as the operations base.
Ground vehicles and helicopters must be built at the operations base. Fixed-wing construction is also enabled at FOBs.
Vehicles, helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft must be built at the operations base.

A campaign you have to sustain
Frontline Liberation is a persistent cooperative campaign. Take occupied territory, protect what you hold, and keep your force supplied. The enemy fields garrisons, patrols, reserves, artillery and logistics with finite stocks. Your choices affect what it can send next.

The campaign loop
Reconnoitre an objective. Bring the troops and equipment to take it. Secure the approaches, recover useful supplies and prisoners, then prepare for the response. A successful assault is only part of the job; transport, medical support and defending the rear keep the advance moving.

Your current victory condition
%1. Check Mission Parameters in the map diary for the active campaign settings.

Use this field guide
Select a chapter or use Previous and Next. Scroll inside the reading panel when needed. Reopen How to Play from your action menu during play. The guide remembers your chapter for this session.

1. Join your squad
Choose a role, complete the introduction and select an available deployment point. The operations base is your starting hub. Check the map and coordinate with your squad leader before choosing a forward location.

2. Equip for a specific job
Use the available arsenal and supply sources. Bring compatible magazines, medical supplies and the tools your role needs. Confirm the server's ACE interaction, self-interaction and radio bindings. Keep enough carrying capacity for the work ahead.

3. Plan the return trip
Arrange transport, casualty evacuation and a way to recover prisoners or resource crates. Check fuel and ammunition before leaving. Nearby does not mean undefended: watch roads, ridgelines and the route behind you.

4. Move as a team
Choose a manageable objective, observe it before committing, and assign security while others work. Infantry, vehicles and logistics serve different jobs. If an action is unavailable, check your distance, vehicle state, permissions and the message shown on screen.

Put troops on the objective
Sector ownership is decided by eligible troops around the sector marker, within %1 m. At the time this page opened, the minimum friendly presence is %2; it scales with connected players. This is a minimum, not a guarantee: the balance of friendly and enemy troops also matters. Bring ground troops and clear remaining resistance.

Confirm the result
Watch the sector marker and capture notification. Check buildings, approaches and nearby cover for survivors. Capturing a sector removes it from the enemy supply network and clears its remaining enemy reserve stock. Deployed enemies elsewhere do not disappear.

Keep what you take
Enemy formations can retake friendly sectors and threaten your bases. The attack countdowns on the HUD and map concern enemy capture of friendly objectives. Contesting an area can pause progress; a zero timer can still be waiting for enemy control. Respond to the objective and its status, not just the clock.

Secure before moving on
Leave observation or a reaction plan behind. Recover supplies and prisoners while another team watches the approaches. A captured marker alone is not protection for an unattended logistics convoy.

Towns and the wider front
Ordinary sectors expand friendly territory and remove enemy supply nodes. Capturing a link can interrupt a route, but alternate routes may remain. Plan a useful line of advance and protect the roads you need for your own hauling.

Military bases and major towns
These are campaign strongpoints. Held military-sector count unlocks parts of the construction catalog; read each item's actual requirement in the build menu. Your active victory setting determines which objectives must be held to finish the campaign.

Factories
Factory depots hold an organized cache of physical resource pallets. Secure the yard and recover surviving cargo with trucks and storage. The initial cache is finite: destroyed or recovered pallets do not reappear when you recapture the factory. Ongoing production is separate and needs a friendly facility with storage. Check the Resources and Production chapters before committing trucks.

Radio towers
Decide before the assault whether you want a working interception site or a temporary disruption of enemy coordination. Capturing an intact tower and destroying an enemy-held tower have different consequences. Read the next chapters and brief your demolition team.

Forces have a cost
Garrisons, patrols, reinforcements, vehicles and support draw on enemy manpower and equipment. Reserves move between objectives and the enemy can rebuild losses while it has stock. Its shared off-map reserve replenishes up to %1 percent of capacity every %2 minutes of mission time; reserves are finite, but waiting can give it time to recover.

Expect a response beyond the sector
Reconnaissance, ambushes, motorized forces and helicopter insertions can threaten your route or reinforce another fight. Insertion helicopters land troops; those troops continue fighting after the carrier leaves. A quiet approach does not promise a quiet withdrawal.

Break observation
Enemy observers and reports feed its response. Artillery observers can improve their solution while maintaining contact. Move, use cover and break line of sight when taking fire. This reduces useful observation; it does not cancel shells already in flight or guarantee safety.

Support has counters
Your guns can draw counterbattery attention. Aircraft can meet radar and air defenses. Sustained, reported infantry assaults near enemy objectives can also draw attack helicopters or jets when the enemy has aircraft reserves. Their guns, explosive rockets and bombs threaten troops on foot. Once observed, ducking behind a tree or into a building does not cancel a committed strike: the aircraft can attack your last seen position, and the ammunition can damage that cover. Move away from that position while concealed; lost observation prevents precise tracking through cover. Use reconnaissance and dated intelligence to plan around support assets, and attack their supplies or source operations when the opportunity arises.

Capture intact: gain reports
Hold a functioning tower to intercept enemy activity. Interception attempts occur roughly every %1-%2 minutes and depend on real activity being available. Reports are dated clues, not a continuous view of every enemy. A quiet period may produce no useful report.

Destroy enemy-held: disrupt coordination
Destroying an enemy-held tower slows enemy command coordination for %3 minutes. Coordination intervals are multiplied by %4 during that window. Existing movement, fighting and committed salvos continue, so keep covering the assault and withdrawal.

Understand the trade
Further qualifying tower destruction refreshes the disruption window instead of stacking a stronger multiplier. The enemy reroutes communications when the window expires. A ruined tower cannot intercept, and there is no player repair action to restore it.

Check ownership and status
Destroying a tower already held by your side does not earn the enemy disruption effect. Read the tower marker: INTERCEPTING identifies a working friendly site; DESTROYED identifies a ruin. Coordinate explosives before your team captures the sector.

Read intelligence on the map
Open the map and hover an intelligence marker to read its source, age and details. Click a marker to show its recorded route; click again to clear it. Overlapping markers cycle through their reports. Assigned operations remain in the normal map task list. Prisoners, recovered documents, civilian informants and functioning friendly radio towers provide information through different opportunities.

Read what the source actually knows
Reports can describe troop dispositions, artillery, fire plans, fortifications, convoys, air defenses or stock. Positions and estimates describe the report's observation; they are not live tracking. Reconfirm old information before committing a team.

Separate reserves from forces in the field
Enemy stock reports describe uncommitted reserves. Fielded soldiers and vehicles are separate, and active convoy cargo is reported separately from sector stock. A low reserve figure does not mean the nearby battlefield is empty.

Turn information into a plan
Use reports to choose reconnaissance routes, avoid prepared fire areas and find support targets. Military bases keep a records desk inside a building near the objective, with a small field office where no suitable room exists. Use ACE interaction and Collect intelligence on its papers to recover stock ledgers for the base and up to four other enemy objectives in its connected supply network, plus up to six related operation reports. Convoy endpoints and nearby supply links take priority. Each reported objective has its own dated stock marker on the map. Search before demolishing the buildings: destroyed or collected records do not respawn. Capturing the base preserves the dossier's last recorded stock figures, not live access to its network. Other sources can open linked operations automatically. There are no intelligence points to earn or spend and no purchased coverage. Reading an ordinary report does not guarantee a new mission.

Take custody
Enemy survivors may surrender. Use ACE interaction and Escort to FOB / patrol base. The prisoner joins your squad; use normal squad movement, stop and vehicle orders to manage the journey. Keep the escort together. Abandoned prisoners can escape.

Return alive
Bring the prisoner to a friendly FOB or patrol base and dismount there together. Once detained, they remain physically at the site. Delivery alone gives no information. Protect the prisoner from fire and arrange transport before an assault likely to yield captives.

Conduct the interrogation
Approach on foot and select Interrogate prisoner. Stay at the same base, within %1 m, for %2 seconds. Both you and the prisoner must remain conscious. Leaving or becoming incapacitated interrupts the attempt; return and try again if the source survives.

Use the result
Ordinary prisoners provide a source report. Their chance to offer a difficult linked operation is %3 percent, subject to an eligible case and available enemy resources. A report is useful even when no chain opens. An identified HVT has its own required detention step, explained next.

Follow each assigned stage
An eligible source can open a defended chain. Stages are assigned automatically as you progress. Read the task, location and deadline. A stage may wait while its site and defenders are prepared; follow the case state rather than assuming an empty marker is complete.

Documents, then a live HVT
First search the defended building and use Collect intelligence on the dispatch documents. Next locate the identified HVT and clear the nearby guards. Use Detain HVT even if you have already restrained them with ACE. Escort them alive to a FOB or patrol base and interrogate them.

Strike the revealed support site
At the final compound, use Sabotage support site on the marked equipment, or destroy it. Expect interior guards, patrols and crewed emplacements. Dead HVTs, destroyed evidence and expired stages can end a chain.

Know the operational effect
A supply raid removes %1 percent of the source sector's remaining manpower, supplies, rockets and transport stock. A fire-control raid interrupts new artillery support funded by that source for %2 minutes. A command raid delays new ground formations from that source for the same period. Existing forces and committed salvos continue.

Three construction resources
Supplies, ammunition and fuel pay for construction. They exist as physical cargo. Recover crates, carry them to the base that needs them and store them correctly. The local/global resource HUD toggle changes what you see; it does not move resources between bases.

Load and recover
Use the available Load box and Unload box actions on compatible logistics vehicles. ACE cargo is another option where the vehicle and object support it. Check capacity and bring a vehicle that can carry the actual load. Protect the loading area before stopping a truck there.

Store deliberately
Use the storage actions to store or retrieve pallets, and Check value when you need to inspect a resource crate. Parking cargo beside a platform is not the same as storing it. Keep loading lanes clear and avoid mixing stock intended for different forward bases.

Keep the two supply systems clear
Construction-resource crates pay for assets. Squad resupply crates hold usable magazines, weapons, medical items and equipment. A crate full of rifle magazines is not automatically construction ammunition. Plan both the campaign haul and your squad's immediate combat load.

Set up a productive site
At a friendly production sector, establish the required sector storage and select the resource you need. Building storage requires Building permission; managing production requires Production permission. Check the management display for the active selection, facility state and capacity.

Collect what you make
Production creates physical stock over time and needs room in storage. A full facility cannot keep filling indefinitely. Arrange regular collections and move output to a useful base. Production advances while players are present, and poor civilian reputation slows it.

Recover useful vehicles
With Recycling permission, inspect an eligible empty vehicle and use SALVAGE VEHICLE. Read the displayed yield before confirming. Condition, remaining ammunition and fuel affect recovery. Wrecks return supplies rather than their old combat load.

Choose where to salvage
A recycling depot improves recovery. Field salvage produces loose resource crates at a lower yield, so bring transport and secure the area. Captured enemy equipment can be valuable. Decide whether the team needs the working asset more than the materials you would recover.

Get access and bring stock
Building permission is assigned by an administrator. On foot, open the build menu within %1 m of your operations base or FOB. Read costs, military-sector unlocks and capacity limits before choosing an item. Nearby hostiles and an invalid placement can prevent construction.

Use the current vehicle policy
%2 Air assets also depend on the relevant unlocks and available facilities or capacity shown by the build menu.

Establish another FOB
Use an available FOB container or FOB truck from the logistics system. Move it to a valid site and deploy on foot with Building permission. Allow at least 1,000 m from other FOBs and the starting base, and 300 m from sector markers. The campaign also limits the total number of FOBs.

Build a base you can sustain
Choose truck access, room for storage and a defensible approach. Supply the new FOB before expecting to build there. Do not scatter expensive assets where one attack can destroy them. Use the provided repack and relocation actions when consolidating a position.

A small forward foothold
A friendly group leader can use ACE self-interaction: Place PB. The campaign permits %1 patrol base(s). Placement needs suitable clear ground, at least %2 m from a FOB or the starting base, and %3 m from hostile sectors. A PB supports forward deployment and prisoner delivery; use a FOB for construction and resource infrastructure.

Plan before placing
Dismantling is locked for %4 minutes after placement. When that lock expires, a group leader on foot within %5 m can use Dismantle PB. You can place a replacement after dismantling; its own placement starts a new lock.

Redeploy from a valid location
Use Redeploy when available near the operations base, a FOB, a patrol base or an eligible mobile respawn. Be on foot and select an available destination. Redeploy is a base-to-base tool; it is not an extraction action available anywhere in the field.

Keep an alternative
Enemy pressure can make forward destinations unavailable. Mobile respawns can have a deployment delay and need protection. Keep a transport or fallback plan in case the point you intended to use is attacked or lost.

Use a supply source
ACE-interact with a supported supply source and open Resupply Crates. Choose Grab for the crate type you need, then move it to your squad. Available choices and specialist allocations depend on your role and the configured source.

Share the squad allowance
Ordinary crate limits follow your current Arma group and its connected players. The menu shows allocation and cooldown information. Coordinate requests inside the squad so one person does not occupy the available crates with equipment nobody needs.

Return, refill or recall
Bring crates back near a valid source to use the return or refill actions when available. Recall ALL removes issued crates: tell teammates before recalling something they are using. Follow the menu's distance and cooldown messages if a request is rejected.

Prepare for the actual deployment
Check the contents and take compatible ammunition, medical supplies and tools. Load transport before moving out and keep track of where you leave the crates. This system equips the squad; it does not replace hauling the physical resources needed to build campaign assets.

Use the server's medical system
ACE medical settings and installed extensions determine treatment. Know your role and the available interaction menus before contact. Move casualties out of immediate danger, coordinate with qualified medical players and arrange evacuation when field care is not enough.

Deploy a field hospital
Doctor-qualified players can use Deploy Field Hospital through ACE self-interaction on suitable terrain. Each doctor can have one deployed hospital and must repack it before placing another. Use Repack Field Hospital nearby when moving your facility. A medical facility is not automatically a respawn or redeploy point.

Protect civilians and property
Identify targets and control explosives around populated areas. Harming civilians or their property damages civilian reputation, which can slow your production. Clearing an objective while preserving its people and infrastructure supports the campaign beyond the immediate fight.

Listen to local sources
Civilian informants can provide intelligence. Follow the contact opportunity, secure the area and escort the informant as directed to a FOB or patrol base. Keep them alive and respect the task deadline. Their report can help even when it does not produce a linked operation.

Split the work
Infantry secures the objective, support watches likely responses, logistics recovers stock and prisoners, and medical personnel keep the team in the fight. Assign these jobs before contact. Brief a withdrawal route and who will remain to cover loading or treatment.

Permissions are separate from rank
An administrator assigns Building, Recycling and Production permissions. Choosing the commander slot or leading a squad does not automatically grant them. If a campaign action is missing, check permission first, then location, resources and the conditions shown by the menu.

Use command tools where enabled
Players operate the vehicles they build. AI recruitment, crewed purchases and AI support commands are unavailable. Use Zeus with your configured bindings when enabled; vehicles still need the resources, space and facilities required by their construction options.

Keep the team informed
Use the installed radio system and agree on channels and callsigns. Report sightings with a position, time and direction of travel. Distinguish current observation from an old intelligence report. Reassess after every capture: what changed, what can the enemy still do, and what does the next team need?
You have liberated the area from the enemy oppression.
